title: Introduce backpressure, priority routing and staged degradation for rerank endpoints
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: reduce tail latency and improve availability of the reranker endpoint under high ingestion while preserving quality. Implement server-side backpressure, prioritized request queues, adaptive timeouts and a staged degradation policy that falls back to cheaper approximate reranking (embedding-similarity or small reranker model) when the primary reranker is overloaded. Add per-region circuit breakers and regional routing preferences so regional outages or capacity pressure do not cause global failures. Deliverables include implementation, load tests, dashboards, canary rollout plan, and a rollback/fallback playbook.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Under target 5% p99 load spike, p99 latency improves by >=20% compared to baseline or staged-degradation is triggered with documented fallbacks. 2) Circuit breaker trips and automatic fallback on simulated regional GPU degradation in >90% of simulations. 3) End-to-end integration tests for prioritized queues, per-customer limits, and fallback correctness green in CI. 4) Console exposes per-route metrics and a playbook for manual override of fallback routing.
implementation_notes: - Add three priority queues (high/normal/low) in the ingress path with capacity-weighted dequeue. - Implement token-bucket backpressure and soft queue limits per-API-key to avoid noisy neighbors. - Adaptive timeout: scale request timeout based on recent observed latency per-region and per-model. - Circuit breakers per-region+model with exponential backoff and safe open-window. - Fallbacks: order of fallbacks = lightweight embedding-similarity rerank -> quantized small reranker -> degraded result with warning. - Add feature flag and rollout gating by customer tier to test behavior on low-risk tenants first.
test_plan: 1) Synthetic load test (k6) to validate p50/p95/p99 under stepped traffic; compare with baseline. 2) Chaos tests that degrade GPU pool in a region and validate regional circuit breaker triggers and routing fallback. 3) Regression tests for rerank result ordering using canonical evaluation set; measure MAP@k and NDCG. 4) Per-tenant spike tests to verify per-customer soft limits and backpressure behavior. 5) CI unit tests for queueing logic and integration tests for fallback correctness.
risk_mitigation: - Start with conservative thresholds and long open-window for new circuit breakers. - Rollout to internal canary org then to tiered beta customers. - Keep logs of fallback decisions and add debug flags to force primary path. - Add automated revert if p99 latency or error-rate exceeds thresholds during canary.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy server changes behind feature flag. 2) Canary on internal traffic for 48h, monitor p95/p99, error-rate, and quality metrics. 3) Enable for 10% of customers for 72h. 4) Expand to all non-enterprise customers, then enterprise after manual sign-off. 5) Full rollout with accompanying docs and runbook.
monitoring_and_metrics: Create dashboards: rerank-ingress-queues (occupancy by priority), rerank-pipeline-latency (per-region, per-model), fallback-rate, circuit-breaker-state, per-api-key drop-rate, quality-regressions (MAP@10 daily). Export structured logs for each fallback decision with reason code.
comments: 2026-02-16: Spike experiment: initial in-memory priority queue prototype reduced p99 by ~18% on small scale but increased p50 slightly due to head-of-line blocking for low priority traffic.
2026-02-22: Decided to add per-API-key soft limits to avoid noisy neighbor issues; this requires token-bucket integration with rate limiter service. Assigned integration to ENG-13900.
2026-02-28: Implemented adaptive timeout heuristic that uses EWMA of regional latency; initial tests show fewer false-positive circuit opens.

2026-03-03: Design review feedback from PM: need explicit SLA-preserving behavior for enterprise-tier customers — added priority override and guaranteed reservation path. Update in implementation_notes.

2026-03-08: Load test (k6) with 5x baseline traffic: fallback rate peaked at 12% and quality drop was within tolerance for non-beta tenants. Observed a regression in MAP@10 for one dataset — flagged for follow-up with ML team.
2026-03-10: PR opened for queueing layer and circuit breaker: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/1492; security review scheduled next week.
open_tasks: Address MAP@10 regression with ML team and add guardrails in fallback selection
Add per-customer SLA override path and manual toggle in console
Finalize canary schedule and alert thresholds
estimated_impact: Reduce global p99 latency tail and improve availability during regional capacity pressure, with controlled quality trade-offs via staged fallbacks. Expected to reduce incident surface from reranker overloads by ~70% based on simulations.
